text: A released offer is dispatched by this service's own event, rwb.treatment.TreatmentApproved.v1 (EV-10) on rwb.treatment.events.v1 with key caseId, consumed by rwb-comms to issue the letter on the consented channel and by rwb-payment to expect the money; the event carries facts and identifiers only, and the letter's addressee is resolved by rwb-comms, so rwb-treatment reads no v_ace_* view and adds no contract dependency for the send.
why: FSD A2.7.2 names Workbench, WIN, NSS and LINE OA as integration points with no contract, Architecture v5 slide 13 shows no REST line from S2 to P6 and shows rwb-comms listening to S2's events, and the legacy story's own data table names v_ace_customer while Architecture v5 slide 8 gives the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views to rwb-source-data alone.
read: Architecture v5 slide 13 (S2 Treatment row and P6 Comms row) and slide 42 row 10 (event 10); slide 8 notes on the v_ace_* views; TSD S2 v2 T5.3 (TreatmentApproved, published); FSD S2 v3 A2.7.2; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-05 and DP-09, R7.2 s17
applied_in: RWB-S2-E3007-APP sections 4, 7, 11, 12.3 and 12.8; RWB-S2-E3007-CON sections 7 (AC3), 8, 12.3 and 12.8
confirm: P6 owner of the letter with the rwb-treatment tech lead and the P1 owner of the ACE views at the wave 2 contract freeze
impact: If rwb-comms cannot resolve the addressee on its own path, rwb-treatment needs a customer read through rwb-source-data's contract and a C dependency appears on the story; the event body and the criteria do not change.

text: The case status, the assignment and the case-level clocks stay rwb-case's. rwb-treatment reports the stage outcome of R-RES-04 and R-RES-11 to the parent CaseWorkflow, the parent moves the status, and this story reads no recovery_case, assignment or timer row.
why: Both acceptance criteria of the legacy story that name a case state end with a status move (WITH_FCR_OFFICER, OFFER_WITH_CUSTOMER), while Architecture v5 slide 41 gives the case and its state to rwb-case, DP-01 forbids reading another service's tables, and the Work Package lists no contract dependency that a case REST call would need.
read: Architecture v5 slide 41 (rwb-case owns the case, its state, queues, tasks and timers) and slide 18 (S2 rwb-treatment); Temporal and Drools Design slides 13 and 14 (CaseWorkflow is the parent and each stage a child); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01
applied_in: RWB-S2-E3007-APP sections 4, 7 Target reading, 9 State transitions and 12.7; RWB-S2-E3007-CON sections 8 (BR11) and 12.8
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-treatment with the P3 owner of the case workflow at the wave 2 build start
impact: If the parent does not own the transition, a stage would have to signal rwb-case over REST and a C dependency would appear on the plan; no business rule changes either way.

text: The offer-preparation clock of R-RES-04 and the offer validity of R-RES-11 are values in force, and both are durable Temporal timers inside TreatmentWorkflow rather than timer rows or Schedules: the routing workbook gives two working days for the R-RES-04 clock and fourteen days for the offer validity, and this run exports them as parameter keys without fixing their values in code.
why: Nine acceptance criteria of the service end with a clock or a validity date, the routing workbook carries both periods in its service-level column only, Architecture v5 slide 42 retires the TimerDue event because the clock lives inside the workflow, and no parameter key is defined by any source document.
read: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-04 ('2 working days') and R-RES-09, R-RES-11 and R-SET-06 ('offer validity 14 days'); Temporal and Drools Design slide 18 ('Offer sent, valid 14 days', 'Clocks: Offer 14 days') and slide 13 step 4; Architecture v5 slide 42 event 18; FSD S2 v3 A2.7.3.1 BR-S2-007
applied_in: RWB-S2-E3007-APP sections 3, 4, 7 Target reading, 8 (BR4 to BR6), 12.5 and 13; RWB-S2-E3007-CON sections 7 (AC2 and AC4), 8 (BR2, BR3, BR7) and 12.6
confirm: P3 owner of the parameters with the rwb-treatment tech lead at the wave 2 build start
impact: If the parameter set cannot carry the two periods, they become reference-data rows of the rule package; the criteria hold either way, because none of them names a number.

text: The release of an offer rides the offer operation that RWB-S2-E3002-CON publishes on base /api/recovery/treatment/v1 and declares no path of its own; its body is OfferRelease with six properties and three required, of which five map to treatment fields and releasedAt is a request-context fact recorded on the decision record, because TSD S2 T3.1 gives the release instant no column.
why: The legacy story's endpoint table lists only the treatment read and the treatment submit, Architecture v5 slide 18 names POST /treatments/{id}/offer, TSD T-A.1 API-S2-004 names the submit form, and no source publishes a release body, a required set or a column for the send instant.
read: Architecture v5 slide 18 (rwb-treatment IN, POST /treatments/{id}/offer); TSD S2 v2 T-A.1 API-S2-004 and T3.1 (DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033); legacy RWB-E3-007 section 19 (endpoint table) and section 11 (data table); Template and Rules v1 R3 source precedence and R5.5 DP-13
